svg.title: Japan at a glance — static SVG infographic
svg.desc: One-page infographic about Japan: stylized map with Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka and Nagoya; nominal GDP bar chart 2015–2024; population donut chart by nationality; and top destinations.
svg.text: Geography · economy · people · travel — a 2024 snapshot
An island nation in East Asia, Japan arcs about 3,000 km
from the Sea of Okhotsk to the East China Sea. Four main
islands — Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu — are home to
nearly all of its ≈125 million people.
Capital & largest city — Tokyo (≈37 m in Greater Tokyo)
Shinkansen — bullet trains up to 320 km/h
Culture — washoku cuisine, anime, manga, craft
Constitutional monarchy · parliamentary democracy — Emperor Naruhito is head of
state; the Prime Minister leads the government.
An island nation in East Asia, Japan arcs ~3,000 km across some 6,800 islands — four main ones (Hokkaido, Honshu,
Shikoku, Kyushu) hold almost all of its ≈125 million people. It blends deep tradition with frontier tech, and stays
a top-five economy: nominal GDP ≈ US$4.0 tn (2024). Below: cities, GDP trend, population mix, and places to visit.
Fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP — about
US$4.03 trillion in 2024, behind the US, China
In US-dollar terms output peaked at US$5.12 tn
(2019); since 2022 the weaker yen has pulled the
dollar figure down, even as yen-denominated GDP
Exports ≈ 20% of GDP — cars, machinery, chips
current US$ trillions · source: IMF WEO
2019 peak US$5.12 tn → 2024 US$4.03 tn; the fall is mostly yen weakness (¥110→¥151/US$ in 2022–24).
Foreign nationals ≈ 2.5% of residents; Chinese, Vietnamese and South Koreans are the
largest groups. Japan is among the world’s most homogeneous societies.
Sources: IMF World Economic Outlook (nominal GDP, current US$) · Statistics Bureau of Japan & Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (population by nationality, 2024 est.)
Map stylized, not to scale; city positions approximate. Figures rounded. Self-contained static SVG — no JavaScript, no external assets, no raster images.
